name: Enalapril
executiveSummary: ACE inhibitor. Adult HTN: **5–20 mg PO/day** (up to **40 mg/day** in 1–2 doses). HF: start **2.5 mg** 1–2×/day, titrate. Pediatrics: **0.08–0.6 mg/kg/day**. IV enalaprilat: **0.625–1.25 mg q6h**. Contraindicated in pregnancy.
indications:
## Indications

- Hypertension; heart failure; post-MI LV dysfunction; diabetic nephropathy (context).

## Precautions

- First-dose hypotension (hypovolemia/diuretics).
- ↑ K+, ↑ creatinine — monitor; bilateral renal-artery stenosis.
- Dry cough; angioedema (stop and do not rechallenge).
- **Teratogenic** — stop if pregnancy.

> Enalaprilat = active IV metabolite.

adulto.dose: HTN: start **5 mg/day** (or **2.5** if hypotension risk); usual **10–20 mg/day**; max **40 mg/day**. HF: **2.5 mg** 1–2×/day → titrate to **10–20 mg q12h**. IV enalaprilat: **0.625–1.25 mg q6h** (max **5 mg/6 h**).

pediatrico.dose: PO start **0.08 mg/kg/day** (max start 5 mg); range **0.1–0.5 mg/kg/day** in 1–2 doses; max <12 y **0.6 mg/kg/day**; ≥12 y up to **40 mg/day**. IV enalaprilat: **5–10 µg/kg** q8–24h.

neonatal.dose: Neonatology/cardiology only — risk of severe renal failure.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hypotension, cough, hyperkalemia, ↑ creatinine, dizziness; rare: angioedema, agranulocytosis.
